watch_next: The Senate budget and the final state budget, which the minutes expect in early July, will settle the circuit breaker and Chapter 70 figures behind the school budget.
A future agenda discussion on district-wide proof of residency was requested at the end of the meeting.

what_happened.line: The superintendent presented a level-service school operating budget for next year, and a motion on its bottom line followed; the result is not audible.
The committee took up the three-year teacher contract agreement with the educators association; a motion was made and seconded, and the result is not audible.
A motion to accept two additional school choice openings in grade 9 was made; the superintendent proposed using that choice money for the ski and lacrosse teams.
Health insurance renewed higher than budgeted, and one-time school choice funds that covered the gap last year must now be absorbed in the budget line.
Three policies went to a third reading and a Town Meeting auditorium food and drink waiver was moved; results for both are not audible.

why_it_matters: The school operating budget is the main school cost the town budget, mostly taxes, is asked to carry, and the contract, health insurance and special education tuition are among the lines that move it.
The state budget is not final, so circuit breaker and Chapter 70 aid could change what the district must cover from local sources.
Most votes were taken by voice and the captions do not carry the results, so the outcomes need to be checked against the official minutes.

what_happened.line: The School Committee gave final approval to the K-8 English language arts curriculum on its third reading.
After a long calendar debate, the committee settled on an interest-based workshop instead of revisiting the 2017-18 calendar.
The committee approved line-item transfers for fuel oil after a power outage, for paper supplies, and for security cameras at two schools.
The committee voted to approve North Middlesex joining the collaborative.
The committee gave initial approval to a Nashville music trip, with per-student cost described as tentative pending pricing.

why_it_matters: The transfers move money inside the school budget for fuel, supplies and building security, and the Nashville trip's per-student cost could fall on families if it stays high.
The ELA curriculum is now approved for every K-8 classroom, and the calendar workshop will shape future school-year dates for families.
watch_next: The interest-based school calendar workshop the committee agreed to hold.
Second reading of the athletic advisory council, school lunch and facilities use policies, and final pricing and approval for the Nashville trip.
